Waves and fields

Interference & phasors

From the figure to the physics

Fig. 1 shows why coherent fields must be added before their squared magnitude gives power.

For equally polarized coherent waves in the same medium, complex field amplitudes add: Etotal = 1 + aeʲδ. Power is proportional to the squared magnitude of their sum.

Expanding gives |Etotal|² = 1 + a² + 2a cos δ. The cross term carries the phase-sensitive reinforcement or cancellation.

Equal in-phase fields produce four times one wave's local intensity. An absolute power argument must still account for source references and spatial redistribution. At exact cancellation, the zero resultant has no defined phase.

Example

For a = 1 and δ = 60°, relative power is 1 + 1 + 2 cos60° = 3, referenced to either field alone.

    Practice

    1. Two fields have amplitudes 1 and 0.5 and are 180° apart. What relative power remains?

    Add their signed field amplitudes first, then square.

    The field magnitude is 1 − 0.5 = 0.5, so the relative power is 0.25. Unequal opposing phasors leave a residual field.
